Hi Samir / Nimbus ops team,

Thanks for the productive demo earlier — couple of quick notes while they're fresh and to make the engineering handoff smoother. This thread captures: (1) immediate asks from your team, (2) our recommended Dedicated capacity baseline for your workload, and (3) next steps + a pairing session to finalize autoscale policies.

Summary of what you told us on the call:
- Primary use: high-quality chat + structured tool-calls for clinical summarization (avg request ~650 tokens, with occasional 4k-long summaries).
- Expected steady-state traffic: 30 req/min, peak bursts up to 200 req/min during batch ingest windows.
- Retrieving and reranking embeddings for semantic search in prefetch paths (embedding vector size 1536).
- Security: need VPC + mTLS for control-plane API; logs forwarded to your SIEM.

Redwood starting recommendations (Dedicated):
- Baseline pool: 4 GPUs (A100-80GB equivalent) with a min-replicas=2, max-replicas=8 for autoscale.
- Concurrency: target 6 concurrent requests per GPU for chat-generator workloads (with 1.5k tokens/s effective throughput per GPU for the chosen model family).
- Queueing: per-tenant request queues with a soft queue-depth of 250 and hard cap 1000; priority slotting for tool-calls to avoid timeouts.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeat contexts (expected to reduce tokens per request by ~20% during retries).
- Embeddings: use a separate embedding pool sized for throughput — recommended 2 GPU workers (autoscale 1–4) sized to handle batch embedding throughput; include a small hot cache for top-k reranker candidates.

Attachments: integration checklist (PDF), sample-config.yaml (Redwood route + auth example), throughput-estimates.xlsx (initial math).

Immediate asks for your team:
1) Confirm whether you prefer API key or mTLS for control plane (you mentioned mTLS on the call).
2) Share any compliance docs required for SOC-type ingestion (we'll add to the Private onboarding checklist).
3) Kick off a 60-min pairing session next week (we propose Tue 9/21 10am PT) to finalize concurrency targets and a canary rollout plan.

I'll loop in engineering for the sizing deep-dive after you confirm #1–#3.

Cheers,

Samir — thanks for the questions and for confirming mTLS. Per our internal sizing notes (see answers below) and attached spreadsheet, here are concrete numbers you can use for planning and the pairing agenda. Happy to walk through these in the Tue 9/21 10am PT session; I booked a slot and included a calendar invite.

Inline answers to your ops questions:

A) Latency vs concurrency (approximate; p50/p95 in ms) for the demo model at 650 tokens:
- 1 concurrent on GPU: p50 ~ 110ms, p95 ~ 320ms
- 3 concurrent on GPU: p50 ~ 220ms, p95 ~ 650ms
- 6 concurrent on GPU: p50 ~ 420ms, p95 ~ 1,200ms
Notes: numbers assume quantized kernels and our optimized kv-cache path. Long-tail requests (4k tokens) increase p95 ~3–4x.

Recommendation: target 3–4 concurrent per GPU for steady-state to keep p95 comfortably < 800ms for chat. Allow dedicated low-priority workers (1–2 GPUs) to drain 4k-token jobs or route those into an async pipeline with longer TTL to avoid blocking short tool-calls.

B) For 4k-token tail: put these into a separate low-priority queue with dedicated workers. Configure a throttled admission control so only X long requests can execute concurrently (we suggest 2 concurrent long jobs per pool).

C) Autoscale policy: scale on queue depth + GPU utilization hybrid. Concrete rule we recommend:
- Scale-up trigger: queue-depth > 60 for 45s OR GPU utilization > 72% for 60s.
- Scale-down: sustained queue-depth < 15 and utilization < 35% for 90s.
- Ramp: add 1 replica at a time up to max-replicas; allow burst-buckets for short-term spike handling (burst capacity equal to +20% of max-replicas for <5m windows).

D) Embeddings throughput (1 GPU, mixed precision, batch size 512): ~1.8–2.2k vectors/sec. For daily 50k vector batch, plan for batch windows with 1–2 GPUs for 30–60m depending on overlap with peak API traffic. Real-time upserts are cheap but should be rate-limited to protect embedding pool during ingest windows.

Next steps agreed:
- Confirmed: mTLS for control plane + API keys for app access.
- I attached a sample-config.yaml showing routes for tool-calls, embedding pipeline separation, and queue policy.
- Pairing session: Tue 2027-09-21 10:00–11:00 PT. Calendar invite attached.

If this looks good I'll send a short MUTUAL ACTION PLAN doc with milestones (pairing, canary, scale verification, go-live).
